text:
Priya: quick pulse check  Our dedicated pools still see microbursts where 30 tenants simultaneously oversubscribe and the operator floods the fallback lane. Idea: introduce probabilistic shedding + queued-cohort admission so we avoid synchronized drain.

Owen: probabilistic shedding meaning we randomly drop X% of migrations when load exceeds threshold? need to be careful with SLAs.

Priya: not blind drops. each tenant gets a "cohort score" based on recent usage history, reservation adherence, and latency sensitivity. above a pool pressure threshold, we run a weighted coin flip per-migration where weight = cohort_score. low-score tenants more likely to be shed to fallback or delayed. high-score routes (latency-sensitive) are routed deterministically.

Marco: how is cohort_score computed? sounds complex.

Priya: simple starting formula: cohort_score = clamp( alpha * reservation_utilization + beta * (1 - recent_shed_rate) + gamma * priority_flag, 0, 1 ). alpha/beta/gamma are tunable. keep it opaque to users but expose tier defaults.

Owen: ok. two more pieces: 1) queued-cohort admission where deferred migrations join a short-lived cohort queue with exponential retry & jitter. 2) dynamic pressure threshold that uses rolling-window 95th of pool occupancy instead of instant util to avoid reacting to transients.

Priya: yes. config sketch we can iterate on:
```yaml
shedding_policy:
  pressure_window: 60s
  pressure_percentile: 95
  base_shedding_prob: 0.0
  per_tier:
    enterprise:
      alpha: 0.6
      beta: 0.3
      gamma: 0.1
      min_cohort_score: 0.4
    startup:
      alpha: 0.4
      beta: 0.4
      gamma: 0.2
  queue:
    base_retry: 1s
    max_retries: 6
    jitter: 0.0-1.2s
    cohort_window: 8s
```

Marco: metrics/alerts: cohort_score_histogram, migrations_shed_per_min, cohort_queue_length, pool_pressure_percentile. Alert if migrations_shed_per_min > X and p99 for critical routes increases.

Owen: also add audit trail when shedding occurs: tenant, computed score, random_seed, decision. ops needs this for debugging.

Priya: agree. operator controls: manual_shed(tenant, fraction) and force_admit for emergency. Both require audit and two-step confirmation in console.

deploy-bot: starting canary rollout for feature-flag "prob-cohort-shed-v1" in us-west-1 at 3187654360.

Marco: testing plan: 1) unit tests for scoring math; 2) synthetic load where 100 tenants spike, vary mix of priorities, verify shed rate stabilizes migrations and p99 for gold routes stays constant; 3) chaos run with node failure while cohort queue drains.

Priya: potential failure modes: biased randomness could repeatedly punish same tenant under unlucky seeds. mitigation: include deterministic tie-breaker that rotates seed per-tenant per-window, and make randomness reseed every cohort_window. also add a fairness monitor that flags tenants with repeated sheds > threshold.

Owen: cost/regression analysis: shedding to fallback pool may increase latency and overall GPU-hours depending on fallback efficiency. add cost sweep scenarios in RFC and a safety knob that disables shedding if expected cost delta > X%.

Marco: observability note: cohort_score should be available in traces for sampled requests to correlate with latency changes. expose summary in console.

ops-bot: suggested alert rules: "cohort_queue_backlog" fires if cohort_queue_length > 200 for > 5m (P2), "shedding_fairness_violation" if percent_unfair_tenants > 5% for 30m (P3).

Priya: I'll draft an RFC with math, config defaults, fairness heuristics, and PoC operator patch. tagging @Owen and @Marco for review. Plan: PoC -> small-shard canary -> tuned rollout.

Owen: assign to board "pool-orch-experiments" and drop RFC link here when ready.

deploy-bot: canary completed at 3187654460, no critical errors. telemetry forwarded to #eng-runtime-observability.

Marco: thanks  this feels like a good balance of stability vs SLA protection. Looking forward to RFC.

Priya: thanks team, closing thread to convert notes into RFC.
